source_caption:
To authentically capture the gritty, fading illusion of classic Las Vegas, director Gia Coppola and cinematographer Autumn Durald Arkapaw deliberately chose to shoot The Last Showgirl on 16mm film rather than pristine digital formats. They even utilized custom anamorphic lenses that warped and blurred the extreme edges of the frame, visually reflecting the protagonist’s disorienting, precarious reality as her world slowly collapses. Adding to the tangible authenticity of the production, the cast did not wear newly manufactured wardrobe pieces for their grand stage performances. Instead, they wore actual, extremely heavy vintage showgirl costumes originally designed by the legendary Bob Mackie for the iconic, long-running Vegas revue “Jubilee!”. The painstaking effort to honor the genuine art form provided the film’s lead, Pamela Anderson, with a deeply personal, career-defining role that stripped away her historical media persona in favor of raw, grounded vulnerability.

The Last Showgirl (2024), directed by Gia Coppola, starring Pamela Anderson, Jamie Lee Curtis, Dave Bautista, Kiernan Shipka. A veteran Las Vegas showgirl is forced to confront an uncertain future, navigate her fractured relationship with her estranged daughter, and grapple with a youth-obsessed industry after her long-running revue abruptly announces its closure.

source_details.synopsis: The Last Showgirl is a 2024 American drama film directed by Gia Coppola and written by Kate Gersten. It stars Pamela Anderson, Jamie Lee Curtis, Billie Lourd, Dave Bautista, Brenda Song, and Kiernan Shipka. Its plot focuses on a middle-aged Las Vegas showgirl who is faced with an uncertain future after learning that the revue she has performed in for three decades is scheduled to close. The screenplay was adapted by Gersten from her own play, Body of Work, which she based on her visits to the Jubilee! show shortly before its closure in 2016.
